title: Atoms, Elements and Compounds
summary: The structure of the atom, the first 20 elements of the Periodic Table, chemical symbols and formulae, and the difference between elements, compounds and mixtures.

notes.text: Atoms: the building blocks of matter

All matter is made of tiny particles called **atoms**. Atoms are far too small to see, even with an ordinary microscope. Scientists' ideas about the atom developed over time, from Democritus (about 400 BC), who imagined indivisible particles, to Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr, whose models led to today's picture.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: An atom is neutral because it has the **same number of protons and electrons**. The number of protons (the **atomic number**) tells you which element it is.
A pure substance made of only one kind of atom. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

There are 118 known elements, arranged in the **Periodic Table** in order of atomic number. Each element has a **chemical symbol** of one or two letters: the first is always a capital letter and the second is lower case (Co is cobalt, but CO is carbon monoxide).

items: **Groups** are the vertical columns. Elements in a group have similar properties (Group 1: very reactive metals; Group 18: unreactive noble gases).
**Metals** are on the left and centre, **non-metals** on the right, and **semi-metals** (metalloids) such as silicon lie along the staircase line between them.

notes.text: A pure substance made of two or more different elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. Its properties are different from those of the elements it is made from.
Two or more atoms bonded together, e.g. O₂ (two oxygen atoms) or H₂O (two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom).

notes.title: Reading a chemical formula
notes.problem: How many atoms of each element are in one molecule of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?
steps: The small number after a symbol tells how many atoms of that element there are.
C₆: 6 carbon atoms; H₁₂: 12 hydrogen atoms; O₆: 6 oxygen atoms.
notes.answer: 6 C, 12 H and 6 O: 24 atoms in total

notes.caption: Element, compound or mixture?
rows: Two or more substances, not bonded
Salt water, air, sand and iron filings

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Iron filings and sulfur powder stirred together form a **mixture** (a magnet can pull the iron out). When heated, they react to form iron sulfide, a new **compound** that is not magnetic.

questions.prompt: Which particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
What is the charge on an electron?

questions.explanation: Water is H₂O: hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded. Air and salt water are mixtures.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
Elements in Group 18 (the noble gases) are very reactive.
Match each element to its symbol.
Explain the difference between Co and CO.
questions.memo:
✓ Co (capital C, small o) is the symbol of the element cobalt (1)
✓ CO (two capitals) is the compound carbon monoxide, made of one carbon atom and one oxygen atom (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE differences between a mixture and a compound.
questions.memo:
Any three (1 each):
✓ In a compound the elements are chemically bonded; in a mixture they are not
✓ A compound has a fixed composition; a mixture's composition can vary
✓ A compound can only be separated by chemical means; a mixture by physical means
✓ A compound has different properties from its elements; a mixture keeps the properties of its parts
